reasoning: Cross-section of corn ear shows distinctive pink-red/purple staining of internal cob tissue between kernel attachment sites, which is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot (Fusarium graminearum). Other ear rots show white (Diplodia), yellow-green (Aspergillus), or blue-green (Trichoderma) coloration. The red-pink pigmentation is diagnostic for Gibberella.
